action: No action needed; for awareness. Travellers with disrupted bookings should check rebooking options with their airline.
exec: A network fault at the US air traffic regulator halted flights nationwide; officials say it was not a cyberattack.
plain: On November 13 a telecom network fault stopped flight departures across the United States for several hours. US officials said it was not a cyberattack.
summary: The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop at about 3:54 p.m. ET on November 13, lifted around 8:15 p.m. ET. Officials blamed a router being replaced at a remote site that flooded neighbouring routers; the trigger was undetermined. DHS Secretary Mullin, DNI Jay Clayton and FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia said there was no evidence of a cyberattack. Sen. Duckworth seeks answers on upgrade timing.
title: FAA nationwide ground stop traced to router fault, not cyberattack

validation.note: Two outlets report the router cause and the officials' no-cyberattack statements; FAA's own page was blocked.

review.note: Ground stop 3:54-8:15pm ET Nov 13, router flood cause, Clayton/Raia/Mullin no-cyberattack statements, Duckworth against GovInfoSecurity and ABC7; NBC paywalled
